svg.text: Volleyball Scoreboard: Raspberry Pi (Pi 4 / 3B+) to Arduino MEGA Wiring & Pinout
Verified Hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B (2GB Rev 1.5) | PINK = phone-display UART link (UART2 on GPIO 0/1 needs a Pi 4)

g.text: Ties Pi Ground to Arduino MEGA Ground
GPIO 0 (TXD2) - Phone link: Pi to Arduino
UART2 TX, 38400 baud | 1k series (future phone control)
GPIO 1 (RXD2) - Phone link: score state in
UART2 RX | from Mega TX1 through 10k/20k divider (3.3V)
• Pin 24 (CE0 / GPIO 8) → SSD1351 OLED Chip Select (CS)
• Pin 19 (MOSI) & Pin 23 (SCLK) → OLED Hardware SPI Bus
Mega TX1 is 5V: always via the divider
Digital Input Pins (5V Tolerant, 3.0V+ High Detection)
Connected to Pi Pin 39 (Prevents Floating Signals)
Serial1 RX | from Pi pin 27 through 1k (future phone control)
Pin 18 (TX1) - Phone link: score state out
Serial1 TX, 5V | 10k series, 20k to GND, then Pi pin 28
• Pin 5 → Speaker Audio Out (TMRpcm WAV output)
• Pins A0, A1, A2 → Analog Slider Pots (Bright, Colors)
PHYSICAL PIN LOCATOR: WHERE THE PINS ARE ON THE ACTUAL BOARDS
▲ TOP: MicroSD Slot side | BOTTOM: USB & Ethernet Ports ▼ (header on the right as you look at it)
Row 14, just above the scoreboard cluster (needs dtoverlay=uart2)
1. Orient the board so the USB ports point DOWN.
4. Count rows up from the bottom: row 20 = pins 39/40.
The Golden Rules for your Scoreboard:
• Score wires: LEFT (ODD) column, pins 29 to 39 (GND)
• Pin 40 (yellow) is right across from GND 39
• Phone link: the row ABOVE the cluster:
Building the pink link (5V Mega → 3.3V Pi)
Top edge (USB + power jacks on the left): pins 0-7, then the COMMUNICATION header
labels printed as "TX1 18", "RX1 19" on the board
20 / 21 are already used by the LCD (I²C). Leave them alone.
Double-Row 2x18 Header at the Short Edge of the MEGA (Pins 22–53 + GND)
• Pin 42 = Home Cobra (Orange Wire) | Pin 43 = Away Cobra (Yellow Wire)
• Pin 44 = Spare Wire (Gray Wire) | Pin 45 = Home Score (+1) (Red Wire)
• Pin 46 = Heartbeat (Green Wire) | Pin 47 = Away Score (+1) (Blue Wire)
• Connects to Pi Pin 39 (Bottom-Left Corner GND pin)
💡 Easy Memorization Trick for Arduino Mega:
Count 11 columns in from the left of the 2x18 header to find Pin 42!
Pink link pins 18 / 19 are NOT on this header: see the communication header above.
